'''Monique Combescure''' (born 23 April 1950, née Moulin), is a French [[physicist]] specializing in [[mathematical physics]]. In 2001, she became director of research at the [[Institut national de physique nucléaire et de physique des particules|Lyon Institute of Nuclear Physics]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Institut de Physique Nucleaire de Lyon - Monique Combescure (DR au CNRS) |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=https://www.ipnl.in2p3.fr/spip.php?article127#& |access-date=2022-09-22 |website=archive.wikiwix.com}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> From 2000 to 2008, she was director of the European Mathematics and Quantum Physics Research Group (GDRE MPhiQ) which aims to promote synergy between [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicists]] and [[mathematician]]s in the field of [[Quantum mechanics|quantum physics]]. She received the [[Irène Joliot-Curie Prize|Irène-Joliot-Curie Prize]] in 2007 and the rank of Officer of the [[Ordre national du Mérite|National Order of Merit]] in 2011.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Madame le Professeur Monique COMBESCURE |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=http://www.academiecatholiquedefrance.fr/index.php/qui-sommes-nous/membrescorps-academique/82-section-i-medecine-sciences-de-la-vie-et-de-lunivers/11-madame-le-professeur-monique-combescure#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |access-date=2022-09-22 |website=archive.wikiwix.com}}</ref>

== Life and work ==
In 1970, Combescure joined the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris and decided to devote herself to research in [[theoretical physics]]. She defended her thesis at the [[Paris-Sud University|University of Paris-Sud]] in 1974 on the problem of 3-body quantum scattering under the supervision of [[Jean Ginibre]]. She was then assigned to the theoretical and [[Particle physics|high-energy physics]] laboratory at [[Orsay]]. In 1979 she obtained her doctorate on many-body spectral and scattering problems in [[quantum mechanics]] and [[Quantum field theory|field theory]]. She is a member of the scientific council of the [[Paris-Sud University|University of Paris-Sud]], in particular in the third cycle pedagogy commission (theses and authorizations to direct research).<ref name=":0" />

She has been elected to many research administration bodies, in particular to the Scientific Council of the Mathematics Physics Particles Universe department of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS).<ref name=":0" />

As the Director of the GDRE MPhiQ [[European Research Group]] titled ''Mathematics and Quantum Physics'', she brought together 150 researchers and teacher-researchers working in mathematics or theoretical physics laboratories to explore topical subjects posed by quantum mechanics and field theory.<ref name=":1" />

== Awards ==
Combescure has received several distinctions.<ref name=":0" />
* 1997: Ernest Dechelle Prize from the [[French Academy of Sciences]]
* 2007: [[Irène Joliot-Curie Prize|Irène-Joliot-Curie prize]] for woman scientist of the year
* 2008: Chevalier of the [[Legion of Honour|Legion of Honor]] 
* 2011: Officer of the [[Ordre national du Mérite|National Order of Merit]]

== Selected publications ==
* Combescure, M. (1986). A quantum particle in a quadrupole radio-frequency trap. In ''Annales de l'IHP Physique théorique'' (Vol. 44, No. 3, pp.&nbsp;293–314).
* Combescure, M., & Robert, D. (1997). Semiclassical spreading of quantum wave packets and applications near unstable fixed points of the classical flow. ''Asymptotic Analysis'', ''14''(4), 377–404.
* Combescure, M., Ralston, J., & Robert, D. (1999). A proof of the Gutzwiller semiclassical trace formula using coherent states decomposition. ''Communications in mathematical physics'', ''202''(2), 463–480.
* Combescure, M., Gieres, F., & Kibler, M. (2004). Are N= 1 and N= 2 [[supersymmetric quantum mechanics]] equivalent?. ''Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General'', ''37''(43), 10385.
* Combescure, M. (2009). Block-circulant matrices with circulant blocks, Weil sums, and mutually unbiased bases. II. The prime power case. ''Journal of mathematical physics'', ''50''(3), 032104.
